report.incident_title: Login down for many customers - looks like a network/ISP outage
report.summary: Login requests hung because auth-svc's HikariCP pool was capped at 5 connections by PR #874 (AUTH_DB_POOL_MAX changed from 50 to 5, applied 2026-10-06T11:40Z). Active connections pinned at 5 from 11:40Z while login demand rose from about 81 to about 220 rps. Pending threads for a connection grew from 0 to about 140-151, p99 latency rose from about 125 ms to the 30 s timeout ceiling, and logs show pool timeouts (waiting=143). Confirmed by tool data: the pool cap change and its timing (change record and startup log), pool active/pending metrics, latency, and the pool timeout log. Not confirmed: edge and Cloudflare telemetry was never queried, api-gateway telemetry came back empty, and users-db has only CPU metrics, so the ISP/Cloudflare explanation is refuted by the internal evidence but not checked against edge data. The Cloudflare report shows degraded performance only in the Sao Paulo (GRU) region and does not say which customers route through it, so it should not be posted as the cause. The PR description says minimum idle, but the applied change was the maximum, which should be checked with the identity team.
report.root_cause: PR #874 'Tune DB pool' (identity-team, config change at 2026-10-06T11:40:00Z) set AUTH_DB_POOL_MAX from 50 to 5 in auth-svc. With the cap at 5, auth-svc could run only 5 concurrent DB connections while login demand was about 220 rps. Requests queued for a connection (pending threads rose to about 140-151), waited up to the 30 s pool timeout, and the gateway then logged upstream auth-svc timeouts. This is internal pool exhaustion, not a network or users-db fault.

hypotheses.statement: AUTH_DB_POOL_MAX reduction to 5 in auth-svc at 11:40 Z caused HikariCP pool exhaustion, queuing threads for DB connections and triggering 30 s timeouts, leading to login hangs.

facts.text: auth-svc HikariPool-1 restarted with maximumPoolSize=5, minimumIdle=5 (INFO startup line at 11:41:05Z). This is the only config/startup line found for the pool in 11:00Z-12:45Z.

db_pool_active_connections was 19 at 11:30 and 21 at 11:35, then dropped to 5 at 11:40 and stayed at 5 (the pool cap) through 12:40. Pool was running well above 5 before the change, so the cap of 5 is a real reduction in concurrency.
db_pool_pending_threads (threads waiting for a connection) rose from 0 at 11:40 to 2 at 11:45, 14 at 11:50, 61 at 11:55, 140 at 12:00, and stayed around 146-151 from 12:05 through 12:40.

auth-svc latency_p99 was ~123-126 ms until 11:40, then 410 ms at 11:45, 2900 ms at 11:50, and 30000 ms (the timeout ceiling) from 11:55 through 12:40. The AuthLatencyHigh alert (p99 > 2s) fired at 11:58Z, so latency rose about 13 minutes before the alert.

Log at 12:01:14Z: 'HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=143)'. This shows login requests waiting on DB connections and timing out after 30 s, matching the reported hang of about 15 minutes.

Login request rate rose gradually from 81 rps at 11:30 to about 220 rps by 12:10 and stayed near 217-222 rps through 12:40. Demand roughly tripled while the pool was capped at 5, so queueing is expected.

One log line matches 'login' in 11:30Z-12:30Z: api-gateway WARN at 2026-10-06T12:03:40Z: 'upstream auth-svc response time 30012ms for POST /login'. This is a single entry, and it shows a 30-second upstream wait inside the gateway-to-auth-svc path, after the request has reached api-gateway.
auth-svc db_pool_active_connections was ~19-21 at 11:30-11:35Z, then pinned at 5 from 11:40Z through 12:40Z, matching the AUTH_DB_POOL_MAX=5 change at 11:40Z.

auth-svc db_pool_pending_threads (threads waiting for a DB connection) rose from 0 at 11:40Z to 2 at 11:45Z, 14 at 11:50Z, 61 at 11:55Z, and ~140-151 from 12:00Z through 12:40Z, i.e. requests queue for a pool connection and do not get one.

auth-svc latency_p99 went from ~123-126ms (11:30-11:40Z) to 410ms at 11:45Z, 2900ms at 11:50Z, and 30000ms (timeout ceiling) from 11:55Z through 12:40Z. Login requests per second rose from 81 to ~220 over the same period and then held flat, so load grew before latency did.
Alert AuthLatencyHigh (warning, p99 > 2s) fired on auth-svc at 11:58Z and is still firing. No alerts fired for users-db.

Topology: api-gateway depends on auth-svc and catalog-svc; auth-svc depends on users-db (auth-svc is a JVM service using HikariCP); users-db is a postgres with no downstream dependencies. The login path therefore runs through auth-svc's pool before reaching users-db.

corrective_actions.action: Restore AUTH_DB_POOL_MAX to its previous value of 50 (roll back PR #874) in auth-svc, after confirming users-db has connection headroom, and watch pending threads and login p99 return to baseline.
corrective_actions.rationale: The change record shows the previous value was 50, and the pool cap is the only change in the window. Users-db CPU is about 14-15%, so there is room for more connections. Rolling back removes the queue.

corrective_actions.action: Have the identity team confirm the intended pool setting in PR #874 (minimum idle versus maximum) and set the value deliberately after sizing it against login concurrency and users-db connection limits.
corrective_actions.rationale: The PR description says minimum idle but the applied change set the maximum, so the change did not match its stated intent.

corrective_actions.action: Require load-based sizing review, with the expected peak login rate and users-db connection budget, for any change to auth-svc DB pool settings.
corrective_actions.rationale: A cap of 5 was applied while demand was about 80-220 rps. The change passed without a check of concurrency.

corrective_actions.action: Add alerts on db_pool_pending_threads above 0 for more than a short period and on pool acquisition timeouts, and alert on config changes to pool settings.
corrective_actions.rationale: Pending threads rose from 0 at 11:40Z but the AuthLatencyHigh alert did not fire until 11:58Z, about 18 minutes later. The pool pending metric would have given an earlier signal.

corrective_actions.action: Add per-request timeout and failure logging to auth-svc and api-gateway, and restore api-gateway metrics and traces under the correct service names.
corrective_actions.rationale: Only 3 auth-svc log entries and one gateway WARN appeared in the window, so per-request failure rates could not be measured and gateway-side impact could not be confirmed.
